key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant, because even deep defect levels produce very weak Shockley-Read-Hall recombination due to large lattice reorganizations and suppressed capture rates.
engineering_relevance: For tandem and indoor photovoltaics, t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber whose efficiency limits are unlikely to be dominated by realistic point-defect concentrations.
method: First-principles calculations of a large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium.
Quantified defect-assisted SRH recombination through both nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative capture channels.
Compared recombination trends versus defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions.
evidence_signal: Across the defect dataset, nonradiative recombination was strongly suppressed, with energy release of at least 0.5 Eg per recombination event and radiative defect-assisted capture also too small to explain observed losses.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on point-defect calculations, so device performance could still be influenced by extended defects, interfaces, or extrinsic processing effects not captured here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
